Use spreadsheet tools and AI to compare entered data with source documents and find mismatches faster.
roadmap.project: Process one week of documents with AI capture, log every error type you corrected, and share the top three with your supervisor.

roadmap.title: Become the person who keeps data right
items: Learn data validation: rules, duplicate checks and formats that stop bad data before it enters a system.
Learn spreadsheet skills such as lookups, pivot tables and data cleaning, with AI explaining each step to you.
Document how your team's data flows from paper to system, so errors can be traced back to their source.
roadmap.project: Set up three validation rules in a spreadsheet or system you use, and count the errors they catch over a month.

roadmap.title: Move toward data quality, records or bookkeeping
items: Data quality, records management and bookkeeping use the accuracy you already have and need judgement AI lacks.
Take a short course in one of these areas and ask your manager for tasks in it at work.
Look at related roles: bookkeeping clerk, records clerk or data quality assistant.
roadmap.project: Complete a short bookkeeping or data-quality course and take on one related task at work for a month.

aiTools: AI document capture (OCR) software
Microsoft Excel with Copilot
Data validation rules in your systems
humanEdge: Noticing data that looks wrong in context
Reading unclear handwriting and damaged documents
Careful, consistent accuracy over long tasks

roadmap.title: Work with AI claim and policy processing
items: Use your claims system's document capture to read forms and attachments, and correct the fields it reads wrongly.
Let AI check new applications and claims for missing information, then contact the customer with one clear list.
Draft letters about policy changes and claim status from AI templates, checking amounts and dates before sending.
roadmap.project: Process one month of claims with AI document capture, log every correction you made, and share the patterns with your team lead.

roadmap.title: Fewer errors and faster answers
items: Learn the automated rules that decide which claims go straight through and which come to you, and why.
Keep a log of errors in automated processing and report them so the rules get fixed.
Never put customers' personal or health data into public AI tools; use only your company's approved systems.
roadmap.project: Track for a month which claims the system sent to you for manual review, and suggest two rule changes to your team lead.

roadmap.title: Grow toward customer service and claims handling
items: Get better at calls with customers who are stressed after an accident or loss, explaining clearly what happens next.
Learn the basics of claims assessment to move toward adjuster or examiner work.
Look at related roles: claims adjuster, customer service representative or eligibility interviewer.
roadmap.project: Shadow a claims adjuster for five cases and take over one simple claim from start to finish under supervision.

aiTools: Claims and policy system with document capture
Customer letter templates
ChatGPT or Claude for letters (no personal data)
humanEdge: Helping stressed customers after a loss
Spotting a claim detail that does not fit
Explaining policy rules in plain words

roadmap.title: Hand the routine office writing to AI
items: Draft replies to common customer and colleague questions with AI, then check facts and tone before sending.
Use AI to fill in and proofread forms, expense reports and records, and compare against the source documents.
Ask AI to summarise long documents or email threads so you can answer requests faster.
roadmap.project: Answer 30 routine emails with AI drafts over two weeks, check each one, and count minutes saved and corrections needed.

roadmap.title: Build templates and simple automations
items: Create reusable AI prompts for your most common letters, reports and replies.
Use built-in automation (Power Automate, Zapier or your email rules) to sort incoming mail and requests.
Keep a checklist for what must be checked by a person: names, amounts, dates, personal data.
roadmap.project: Automate one recurring flow, such as filing incoming invoices or logging requests, and document it in a one-page guide for colleagues.

roadmap.title: Become the office's go-to organiser
items: Be the person who knows which tool fits which task, and help colleagues get started.
Strengthen the work AI cannot do: handling difficult callers, judging priorities, keeping things running.
Look at related roles: administrative assistant, office coordinator, or records specialist.
roadmap.project: Teach two colleagues one AI routine you use, and track for a month how much time they say it saves them.

aiTools: Microsoft 365 Copilot or Google Gemini for Workspace
ChatGPT or Claude for drafting and summarising
Power Automate or Zapier for simple workflows
humanEdge: Knowing who to ask and how the office really works
Handling difficult callers with patience
Spotting when a document or request does not look right

roadmap.title: Use the AI already in your cab
items: Learn your navigation and fleet apps well: traffic, restrictions for heavy vehicles, fuel stops.
Use voice assistants hands-free for messages and calls, never touching the phone while driving.
Understand your truck's driver-assist systems and their limits.
roadmap.project: Learn every feature of your fleet and navigation apps for a month and note one thing that saved you time or a detour.

roadmap.title: Less paperwork between loads
items: Keep electronic logs, inspections and delivery records tidy and up to date.
Use AI on your phone during breaks to understand rules, routes or paperwork you are unsure about.
Photograph and scan delivery documents so nothing gets lost.
roadmap.project: Go paperless for one month with digital logs and scanned delivery papers, and count missing or late documents compared with before.

roadmap.title: Grow skills that keep you valuable
items: Keep sharpening what no system does for you: driving in snow or heavy traffic, securing loads, handling customers at delivery.
Learn about new truck technology: electric trucks, driver-assist, remote monitoring.
Look at related roles: driver trainer, dispatcher, or fleet and transport coordinator.
roadmap.project: Take one course on a new skill (dangerous goods, electric trucks, or driver training) and talk to your employer about where it leads.

aiTools: Truck navigation and fleet management apps
Hands-free voice assistant
Electronic logging and document-scanning apps
humanEdge: Driving safely in bad weather and heavy traffic
Securing cargo and checking the truck
Handling customers and problems at delivery
